correspondence.component_scope: Selected northern opening, initial southward feeder and westward approach above Ocoyo
correspondence.finding: The supplied selection begins north and east of the Córdova original and descends through several headward fragments before turning west toward its northern map edge. Neither acquired original covers that opening, its intermediate headward connections or the join into the named downstream valley. Nearby named rivers, discovery prose about Querco and Condorchaca, basin membership and the continuity of the supplied selection are not used to establish these missing through-links.
correspondence.coverage_limit: Materially incomplete. The gap concerns an actual headward branch/corridor and its joining sequence, rather than an unnamed minor tributary or exact source vertex.

correspondence.component_scope: Ocoyo–Santa Teresa/Molinos–Rangra and Sicuay Alto receiving valley
correspondence.finding: The Córdova original depicts Río Grande entering the sheet by Ocoyo, continuing south through Santa Teresa/Molinos, Rangra, Lamari and Chihullo Pampa, and receiving mapped side streams before Sicuay Alto. The selected corridor follows this main valley, including its southwestward bends, rather than the side tributaries. This establishes the mapped receiving valley but not the preceding out-of-sheet headward approach.
correspondence.coverage_limit: Supported at ordinary main-valley and junction scale from the northern neatline near Ocoyo.

correspondence.component_scope: Elipa–Campanario–Huayanga/Pacolla and San Juan del Prieto junction
correspondence.finding: The original follows the named Río Grande past Elipa and Campanario to Huayanga, where the eastern Pacolla drainage enters. Farther south the western San Juan del Prieto drainage converges near Granado and Palomar. The selected continuation stays on the receiving valley through Vado and Ucuchimpana.
correspondence.coverage_limit: Supported continuous corridor and distinct side-stream joins.

correspondence.component_scope: Genovesa–Tucuhuasi–Pinto/Paras and San Jacinto sheet connection
correspondence.finding: The Córdova map follows the selected valley through the Genovesa, Buena Vista, Huambo, San Antonio, Tucuhuasi, La Banda, Pinto and Paras settings, then Gramadal Grande/Chico and San Jacinto. The separate Santa Cruz valley lies to the west and Río Palpa to the east. At the adjacent sheet boundary the same Río Grande corridor continues through the San Jacinto/Florita setting on Palpa. Irrigación Palpa and the reservoirs shown near Santa Cruz are lateral mapped features, not selected crossings.
correspondence.coverage_limit: Supported at regional river-corridor scale, including the shared sheet-edge continuation; no exact bank/datum match asserted.

correspondence.component_scope: Río Grande town–Palpa/Llipata tributary entries and Piedras Gordas
correspondence.finding: The Palpa original follows the named receiving river south past the Río Grande town and Hda. Molino/Dionicio setting, separating it from the easterly Palpa and Viscas approaches. Tributary entries and the continuation through Murive, Arenal, Santa Ana de Llipata, Chillo, Pueblo Nuevo and Piedras Gordas are visible. The selected course remains in the Grande valley through this agricultural reach.
correspondence.coverage_limit: Supported main channel and joining corridors; no scalar name imposed on tributaries or irrigation channels.

correspondence.component_scope: Changuillo-side eastern entry, Santa Cruz confluence and Río Nasca join
correspondence.finding: Below Piedras Gordas the mapped river receives the eastward-lying Changuillo/San Javier drainage corridor and turns southwest past Chiquerillo, Las Mercedes and Cabildo. The separate northern Santa Cruz river joins this receiving course. Farther downstream the Río Nazca-labelled tributary enters near Cerro Colorado/Los Colorados. The original visibly distinguishes those joining approaches and the southward receiving valley; the A53 drainage account calls their convergent lower system Río Grande and places its discharge at the sea.
correspondence.coverage_limit: Supported main-valley continuation and major junctions. Historical map spelling Nazca and report spelling Nasca are preserved as source variants, not competing accepted names.

correspondence.component_scope: Lower desert valley through Coyungo, Las Brujas and Mayo
correspondence.finding: Continuous mapped river hydrography runs south from the Nasca junction past Santa Rosa, Mancha Coyungo, Hda. Coyungo, Los Puquios, Chacra Nueva and Las Brujas, then Panadera and Mayo Chico/Grande. It continues through the Caracoles/Boquerón constriction toward Hda. Monte Grande. The selected lower desert passage is drawn as the river valley; neighboring dry quebradas and pampas are not used as surrogate links.
correspondence.coverage_limit: Supported continuous lower valley at ordinary corridor scale; current seasonal flow, braids and irrigation operation are not established.

correspondence.component_scope: Actual Pacific terminal by Santa Ana/Boquerón and Playa Huasiparita
correspondence.finding: The mapped Río Grande continues from Hda. Monte Grande past Parcona/Mainsa and the Huaticongana-side junction, turns southwest through the Ranca Trapo–Santa Ana setting and reaches the Pacific coast beside Boquerón, north of Playa Huasiparita. The actual coastward connection was read in the original map, not inferred from an inland river label. A53 printed page 7 independently describes the lower Río Grande reaching the sea.
correspondence.coverage_limit: Historical river-to-Pacific correspondence supported; no precise current mouth vertex or shoreline condition asserted.

correspondence.component_scope: Lake, reservoir, canal and hydraulic continuity scope
correspondence.finding: No lake or reservoir passage is identified on the supported Ocoyo-to-Pacific selected corridor. Córdova depicts reservoirs on the separate Santa Cruz side and an Irrigación Palpa feature alongside Río Grande; these are not substituted for the main river. A47 and A53 describe seasonally variable coastal drainage, so drawn channel correspondence is not a present perennial-flow assertion. Waterbody or managed-connector identity in the unresolved northern opening is not inferred.
correspondence.coverage_limit: No positive selected lake/reservoir/managed crossing established on the supported portion. The unresolved opening retains any associated connector question within the single material gap.

correspondence.component_scope: Southern selected opening and northeastern feeder
correspondence.finding: The opening, initial southward turn, eastward return and northeastern feeder have no sufficient acquired primary-map correspondence. No lake, natural source or hydraulic connector is inferred from the selected model alone.

correspondence.component_scope: Upper western course and approach to the mapped eastern middle reach
correspondence.finding: The study figure locates the Aquatuk regional route and distinct lakes, but does not establish the selection’s complete headward path, waterbody entries/exits or wetland through-links. The segment entering the eastern map is covered separately below.

correspondence.component_scope: Eastern middle Aquatuk River
correspondence.finding: The direct Aquatuk label, eastward elbow, northward meandering reach, successive bends, side-stream entries and northwest return to the map boundary correspond to the selection. Nearby ponds and side streams are not renamed. No selected reservoir, glacier or managed connector is established in this inspected interval.

correspondence.finding: Figure 1 joins the named Aquatuk route to Sutton, and field prose separately records sampling in the Aquatuk mouth and along Sutton. This supports the regional receiving relationship, but the general figure and an erroneous printed coordinate do not establish every selected western passage or permit a precise name-change point.

correspondence.component_scope: Lower Sutton River
correspondence.finding: Direct Sutton labelling and the continuously mapped northeastward lower channel, side-stream joins, northward leg, eastward bend and widening estuarine fan correspond at corridor scale. The model’s final generalized leg reaches the outlet’s coastal/intertidal setting. Exact distributary choice, modern banks and tidal limits are not assigned.

correspondence.component_scope: Receiving coastal water and adjacent river context
correspondence.finding: The original map and firsthand field account establish the Hudson Bay receiving setting. Little Cape and the separate Kinushseo River help distinguish this coastal outlet; Kinushseo is not renamed Sutton or appended to the selection.

correspondence.finding: The selected opening lies in the southeastern lake country. CEHQ is too generalized to distinguish the chosen small initial feeder and successive first passages, while RG2013-04 begins farther north. No source-lake name assigned.

correspondence.component_scope: upper_lake_and_stream_chain
correspondence.finding: The northwestward upper selection approaches the regional Lacs Turgis setting on CEHQ. A nearby label does not demonstrate traversal of that lake group or establish each inlet/outlet and branch choice.

correspondence.component_scope: western_bend_and_joins
correspondence.finding: CEHQ depicts the broader northward False corridor separately from western neighboring drainage. It does not distinguish the complete selected westward bend, intervening waterbody connections and joins at the needed corridor scale.

correspondence.component_scope: middle_northward_passages
correspondence.finding: CEHQ supplies regional river and lake context, including the Garreau label. The label is not promoted to a selected lake traversal; complete intermediate connections remain unresolved.

correspondence.component_scope: lower_northward_corridor
correspondence.finding: CEHQ supplies the regional northward False corridor. The northernmost portion is corroborated by GM62436’s Landsat-based lower-river figure, but that figure does not extend through every selected lower interior reach and join south of its image footprint.

correspondence.component_scope: terminal_approach
correspondence.finding: RG2013-04-C001 places the selected northern approach at the distinct southern Kohlmeister-side waterbody east of the Koksoak/Kuujjuaq setting. GM62436 Figure2 shows the winding lower river continuing north into the widened marine-estuary setting, with False River labeled there; its accompanying printed-page6 prose explicitly identifies that outlet. Together these support the selected lower approach and terminal context at ordinary corridor scale. No surveyed mouth vertex, exact bank or present tidal limit is asserted.

correspondence.component_scope: Selected opening and first lake transfer
correspondence.finding: The initial small lake is located relative to named Lac Ammaluttuq and Lac Sirluaq, but the published hydrographic background does not clearly support the first small through-link.

correspondence.component_scope: Eastern intervening lake-and-channel corridor
correspondence.finding: The selected continuation crosses the Vanasse/Belleau study region. Actual report prose and inventory alone do not establish its lake entries, exits or intermediate joins; the separate2057 maps were not read.

correspondence.component_scope: Southern middle dip and approach to Lessard
correspondence.finding: The detailed2088B original shows the eastern lake country and the approach toward Lac Lessard. The review did not establish every selected transfer in the southern dip near the eastern sheet boundary. It is retained as a real geographic gap, not an access failure.

correspondence.component_scope: Lac Lessard passage and northwestward outlet bend
correspondence.finding: The selected middle route passes Lac Lessard and turns northwest into the corridor labelled Rivière Umiruup. This differs from the named Kovik branch approaching from farther southeast.

correspondence.component_scope: Umiruup lower reach and joining Kovik corridor
correspondence.finding: The Umiruup corridor joins the Kovik network near its confluence with the Talluup corridor, and the selected continuation turns west along the mapped Kovik reach north of Lac Chassé.

correspondence.component_scope: Western Kovik channel and lake reaches
correspondence.finding: The western selected course follows much of the labelled Kovik corridor through lake-rich country, including the mapped lower reach near Lac Qamanialuk Tulliq. Short southern-edge portions and their full lake/channel transfers are not all established by this sheet.

correspondence.component_scope: Actual selected sea terminal
correspondence.finding: The last southwestward continuation leaves the detailed map’s southern cartographic coverage. Broad Kovik-region context does not prove the final selected coastal connection. Neither the failed conservation-plan map nor the unavailable coastal study supplies terminal evidence.

correspondence.component_scope: Managed, wetland and ice connectors
correspondence.finding: No managed or glacier connector is positively identified in the read selected-corridor material. Small water/wetland connections and current seasonal or tidal hydraulics are not inferred from the rendered route.
